text:
michael: Customer on PRO reported tool call failing when they pipe JSON from Windows PowerShell. Error: "400 Bad Request - tool args validation failed". They pasted this curl (from customer):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  --data-binary @- <<'PAYLOAD'
{
  "tool": "pdf_extract",
  "args": {
    "path": "C:\Users\Bob\file.pdf",
  },
}
PAYLOAD

michael: note trailing comma after "args" object and windows backslashes. customer says they copied from a doc and pasted into PS terminal.

sam: can you paste the exact raw request body we received (as bytes)? sometimes powershell smartquote or BOM gets inserted. also which SDK/client?

michael: attached raw body (we saved bytes):
EF BB BF 7B 0D 0A 20 20 22 74 6F 6F 6C 22 3A 20 22 70 64 66 5F 65 78 74 72 61 63 74 22 2C 0D 0A 20 20 22 61 72 67 73 22 3A 20 7B 0D 0A 20 20 20 20 22 70 61 74 68 22 3A 20 22 43 3A 5C 5C 55 73 65 72 73 5C 5C 42 6F 62 5C 5C 66 69 6C 65 2E 70 64 66 22 2C 0D 0A 20 20 7D 2C 0D 0A 7D 0D 0A

michael: BOM (EF BB BF) + trailing comma before closing of args. that matches customer paste.

anya: i can repro locally on mac by sending the same bytes (i used echo -e to inject BOM and trailing comma). server returns: "JSON parse error: Unexpected token \u007d in object at position 98" then validation fallback error: "tool args schema mismatch".

sam: thanks. two things: 1) the trailing comma is invalid JSON -> our parser rejects. 2) windows backslashes are fine if escaped correctly (\\) but when pasted into PS some clients convert to single-backslash sequences or smartquotes. the BOM also can confuse some parsers.

michael: customer says they didn't see this until upgrading CLI/ps profile. likely their terminal inserted the BOM or replaced quotes.

anya: quick mitigation we suggested -> instruct customer to: 
- remove trailing commas in JSON (most strict)
- use --data-binary @file.json instead of heredoc in PowerShell
- or wrap payload in triple quotes from a file, or base64 the payload and decode server-side
- example fix (PowerShell):
  $body = Get-Content -Raw .\payload.json -Encoding UTF8
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary $body

sam: can we add a clearer 400 message that points out "invalid JSON (trailing comma or BOM)" so customers know? currently errors are generic schema validation.

anya: i opened an eng-runtime issue and assigned to kai (see issue #INF-4821). suggestion: detect BOM and strip before parse, and return more actionable error when parser fails due to trailing commas. also consider accepting single trailing commas in a permissive mode behind a flag.

kai: i can take a look. quick note: accepting trailing commas silently can hide real issues, but stripping BOM is safe. i'll prototype a pre-parse sanitizer.

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-2026 (linked to INF-4821). Priority: P2 (customer PRO, blocking feature). :rotating_light:

michael: customer wants ETA for workaround. can we reply with explicit copy-paste-safe example and mention BOM/trailing-comma cause?

anya: i'll send a template response and include commands to verify bytes (xxd hexdump) and a fixed sample payload.

kai: assigned, will submit PR with BOM-strip + clearer error by EOD tomorrow, cc eng-runtime.

michael: thanks all :thumbsup:
